title: What San Francisco public bodies pay State lobbyists
question: How much public money does San Francisco spend on lobbyists in Sacramento, through which firms, and which departments pay?
finding: The City ledger shows $6.0 million paid in fiscal years 2019 to 2026 to the 2 firms that hold its State lobbying contracts: Edelstein Gilbert Robson & Smith LLC $3.5 million; Shaw Yoder Antwih Schmelzer & Lange Inc $2.5 million. The paying departments, as the ledger names them, are: Public Utilities Commsn; Mayor; Airport Commission; City Attorney; Municipal Transprtn Agncy. The school district separately reported $587,082 to the State for the same years, which brings the public total on record to $6.6 million; the Transbay Joint Powers Authority also awarded a legislative advocacy contract to 2 firm(s) in 2023 but publishes no amounts.
how: City firms: every prime contract whose title or scope names State lobbying or State legislative advocacy in the City's contract list, then every ledger payment to those firms by department and fiscal year. School district: its quarterly lobbyist-employer reports to the Secretary of State, latest version of each quarter, payment lines added; firm names from its registrations. Transbay authority: its published list of awarded contracts.
limits: The ledger figure is everything the City paid those firms, which could include other advice. The State's lobbying file on disk was cut down to large City payees, so the City's own lobbyist-employer reports to the Secretary of State, which would give the State-side figure and the bills lobbied, are not here; those reports are the record that would supply it. City College has no report under its name after 2007. BART, the transportation authority and the Housing Authority keep their own books, and no vendor ledger of theirs could be found.
